answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. This endures because unearned rewards carry forward into the next pool, so even when a farm fails the economy recycles the loss rather than rewarding it. The effect is that voting power tracks real contribution, so a flood of accounts cannot outvote a smaller set of genuinely established participants. Consider a ivory as the anchor of the cost.
